# Disagreement Log — 1 Clement Chapter 13

**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Agents:** EMET (literal) | LOGOS (formal) | PNEUMA (dynamic)
**Total Disagreements:** 10

---

## Disagreement 1 — 13:1 "humble-minded" vs. "lowly in mind" vs. "humble"

- **EMET:** "be humble-minded"
- **LOGOS:** "be lowly in mind"
- **PNEUMA:** "be humble"
- **Greek:** *tapeinophronēsōmen* — let us be humble-minded
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "be humble-minded" (EMET). The compound *tapeinophronēo* = to think/be minded in humility; the compound should be preserved.

---

## Disagreement 2 — 13:1 "arrogance and conceit and folly and anger" vs. "arrogance and conceit and foolishness and anger"

- **EMET:** "folly"
- **LOGOS:** "foolishness"
- **PNEUMA:** "foolishness"
- **Greek:** *aphrosunē* — foolishness/folly
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "foolishness." Minor; both are acceptable. "Foolishness" is slightly more common in modern usage.

---

## Disagreement 3 — 13:1 Jeremiah citation: "seek him out" vs. "seek him out" vs. "seeking him"

- **EMET/LOGOS:** "to seek him out"
- **PNEUMA:** "in seeking him"
- **Greek (LXX Jer 9:24):** *tou ekzētein auton* — to seek him out
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "to seek him out." Preserves the infinitive of purpose in the LXX.

---

## Disagreement 4 — 13:1 "words of the Lord Jesus" — all agree

- All three agents agree. Recorded. This is a significant phrase — one of the very few explicit attributions to Jesus in 1 Clement.

---

## Disagreement 5 — 13:1 "gentleness and long-suffering" vs. "meekness and long-suffering" vs. "gentleness and patience"

- **EMET:** "teaching gentleness and long-suffering"
- **LOGOS:** "teaching meekness and long-suffering"
- **PNEUMA:** "teaching gentleness and patience"
- **Greek:** *praopathian kai makrothumian* — meekness/gentleness and long-suffering/patience
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "gentleness and long-suffering." *Praopathia* = gentle-suffering/meekness; *makrothumia* = long-suffering (the established term).

---

## Disagreement 6 — 13:2 "Show mercy, that you may obtain mercy" vs. "receive mercy" vs. "receive mercy"

- **EMET:** "obtain mercy"
- **LOGOS/PNEUMA:** "receive mercy"
- **Greek:** *eleate, hina eleēthēte* — have mercy, so that you may be mercied/have mercy shown to you
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "Show mercy, that you may receive mercy." "Receive" is more natural than "obtain" in this context.

---

## Disagreement 7 — 13:2 "As you do, so shall it be done to you" — structural rendering

- **EMET:** "As you do, so shall it be done to you"
- **LOGOS:** "As you do to others, so shall it be done to you"
- **PNEUMA:** "What you do to others will be done to you"
- **Greek:** *hōs poieite, houtō poiēthēsetai humin* — as you do, so shall it be done to you
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "As you do, so shall it be done to you" (EMET). Most literal; "to others" is added by LOGOS without textual basis.

---

## Disagreement 8 — 13:2 "As you are kind, so shall kindness be shown" vs. "As you show kindness"

- **EMET:** "As you are kind, so shall kindness be shown you"
- **LOGOS:** "As you show kindness, so shall kindness be shown to you"
- **PNEUMA:** "The kindness you show is the kindness you will receive"
- **Greek:** *hōs chrēsteueste, houtō chrēsteuethēsetai humin* — as you are kind/good, so kindness shall be shown to you
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "As you show kindness, so shall kindness be shown to you" (LOGOS). "Show kindness" is a natural rendering of *chrēsteuomai*.

---

## Disagreement 9 — 13:2 "With what measure you measure, with the same it shall be measured to you" — phrasing

- **EMET:** "With what measure you measure, with the same it shall be measured to you"
- **LOGOS:** "With the measure you measure, by the same measure it shall be measured to you"
- **PNEUMA:** "Whatever measure you use for others, that same measure will be used for you"
- **Greek:** *en ō metrō metreite, en autō metrēthēsetai humin*
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "With what measure you measure, with the same it shall be measured to you" (EMET). Closest to the Greek and to the standard Gospel rendering (Matt 7:2).

---

## Disagreement 10 — 13:2 Implied subject — all agree on the chiastic structure

- All agents agree on the chiastic/antiphonal structure of the sayings. The ordering in the text is preserved by all three. Recorded.

---

*End of disagreement log for 1 Clement Chapter 13.*
